summary:
Karaya Explorer (Moon Landing Visual) is an interactive web application designed to support the comparison and evaluation of potential lunar landing sites near the Moon's south pole. It focuses on two critical factors for future exploration missions: solar visibility for energy generation and direct visibility of Earth for communication.

The platform integrates an interactive 3D lunar globe, published landing-site coordinates, terrain elevation data, and astronomical position calculations. Users can explore different locations, visualize local terrain horizons, examine sunlight and Earth visibility over time, and compare results through timelines, graphs, and statistical summaries.

Developed using Rust and WebAssembly, the application transforms complex scientific data into accessible visual information. By combining lunar topography, orbital calculations, and interactive visualization, Moon Landing Visual aims to help users better understand the environmental conditions that influence lunar mission planning and the selection of potential landing sites.
details:
Karaya Explorer Moon Landing Visual is an interactive scientific visualization platform developed to help explore and compare potential landing locations near the lunar south pole. The project addresses the importance of identifying locations with favorable environmental conditions for future lunar missions.

How It Works

The application combines several scientific datasets and computational processes to represent lunar surface conditions.

Its main components include:

  • Interactive 3D Moon: Allows users to rotate, zoom in, explore the lunar surface and locate candidate landing sites.
  • Landing Site Comparison: Displays published landing-site coordinates to facilitate geographical exploration.
  • Solar Visibility Analysis: Calculates the visible portion of the Sun from a selected location, helping evaluate potential solar energy availability.
  • Earth Visibility Analysis: Evaluates whether Earth is directly visible above the local terrain, an important factor for communication.
  • Terrain Analysis: Uses lunar elevation data to calculate terrain horizons that can obstruct the Sun or Earth.
  • Timeline and Statistics: Presents visibility conditions over time through visual graphs and statistical summaries.
  • Custom Locations: Supports terrain-horizon calculations for user-selected coordinates.

Scientific Foundation

The project uses astronomical position data from NASA JPL Horizons, lunar elevation models from NASA's LOLA instrument, and NASA Scientific Visualization Studio resources. It combines these datasets with geometric calculations, terrain analysis, and time-dependent visibility computations.

Technology and Tools

  • Rust: Main programming language.
  • WebAssembly: Allows Rust code to run in the browser.
  • WebGL2: Supports interactive 3D rendering.
  • Egui and Eframe: Interface development.
  • NASA JPL Horizons: Astronomical position data.
  • NASA LOLA: Lunar elevation and terrain data.
  • NASA Moon Trek: Lunar imagery and terrain resources.

Innovation and Impact

The main innovation is the integration of lunar terrain, astronomical positions, sunlight availability, and Earth visibility into a single interactive platform. Instead of presenting isolated datasets, the application connects them through visualizations that make complex scientific information easier to explore and interpret.

Its intended impact is to support scientific education, improve understanding of lunar environmental conditions, and provide a visualization tool that can contribute to discussions about future lunar landing-site selection.
